data_authority.rule: This contract does not define tables. Every relation named here must exist in the canonical manifest.

steps: Validate the Supabase JWT and take auth.users.id only from the verified sub claim.
Resolve exactly one enabled core.users row by auth_user_id; auth_user_id is never accepted from an API or MCP argument.
Resolve one active core.memberships row for the requested organization. Organization selection is mandatory when multiple memberships exist and never falls back to the first row.
Resolve optional branch scope against the selected membership and reject unauthorized branches before a domain query.
Join core.access_grants, core.roles, core.role_permissions, and core.permissions; client-supplied roles or permissions are never authoritative.

Call erp_security.activate_context with the verified auth identity and selected organization inside the request transaction; erp_runtime inherits the non-owner erp_app privilege role and every tenant table uses forced RLS.
Reject request-body org_id, created_by, approved_by, auth_user_id, and permission fields when they are server-derived.
identity_resolution_contract.multi_org_rule: A profile is global and a membership is the organization boundary. Switching organization creates a new verified request context and never rewrites the profile.
identity_resolution_contract.failure_mode: Missing, disabled, ambiguous, or unauthorized profile/membership/branch resolution returns 403 before any business query; LIMIT 1 fallbacks are prohibited.

rules: All API and MCP IDs are opaque UUID strings and do not encode tenant, type, sequence, or time semantics.
Nested IDs are accepted only with their parent aggregate ID and are rechecked for the active organization.
Organization and branch headers select verified access and never grant access.
Every mutation returns aggregate_id, row_version, status, request_id, and idempotency replay state.

aggregate_boundaries.reason: Common header fields do not imply a common lifecycle. Conditional mega-table constraints would permit invalid posting and hide command ownership.

aggregates.name: sales_order
aggregates.invariants: revisable until approved; may reserve; never recognizes revenue, GST liability, or journal postings

aggregates.name: dispatch
aggregates.invariants: custody and delivery lifecycle; moves batch stock; may be partially invoiced

aggregates.name: sales_invoice
aggregates.invariants: fiscal and tax snapshot immutable on posting; recognizes receivable, GST and journal effects

aggregates.name: sales_return
aggregates.invariants: batch return cannot exceed invoiced less prior returns; disposition and credit/tax effects are atomic

aggregates.name: purchase_order
aggregates.invariants: approval and open quantity only; no stock, payable, ITC, or journal effect

aggregates.name: goods_receipt
aggregates.invariants: accepted/rejected batch custody and stock; no implied payable or ITC

aggregates.name: supplier_invoice
aggregates.invariants: supplier-number uniqueness, match, payable and ITC snapshot; never duplicates receipt stock

aggregates.name: purchase_return
aggregates.invariants: cannot exceed received batch quantity; stock, debit and ITC reversal effects are atomic

aggregate_boundaries.shared_components: Calculation value objects, response envelopes, numbering, idempotency, audit, outbox, typed source links, and the single calculation.artifacts proof boundary may be shared. Aggregate commands and storage stay distinct.
